title: Fetched facts about index entries
description: data/meta.json, written only by scripts/fetch_meta.py from the GitHub API. Hand-edited only to delete the record of an entry flagged replaced_by, once its new repository has been checked.

exists.description: false when the repository is gone or private, or when replaced_by is set: the site flags the entry.

repo_id.description: GitHub's id of the repository when it was first fetched. It follows the repository through renames and transfers and never passes to another one.

replaced_by.description: Set when the address now holds a repository with a different id: the listed one was deleted and recreated, or its name was taken over. The entry stays unavailable until a maintainer checks it and deletes this entry's record, so the next fetch records the new id.

canonical_repo.description: The repository's current URL, when it was renamed or moved. The index links and imports from here; validate.py asks for the entry file to be updated.

latest_tag.description: The highest release version (v1.2.3, 1.2, v2026.4) among the 100 newest tags, so a backport or a pre-release tagged later does not win; the newest tag by commit date when none is a version. null when untagged, in which case the import line pins the default branch.

latest_tag_commit.description: The commit latest_tag named when it was fetched. Tags can be moved; this cannot.

last_commit.description: Commit date at the head of the default branch.

license.description: SPDX id GitHub detects; 'none' when there is no license file, 'other' when GitHub cannot name it.

upstream_description.description: The project's own GitHub description, kept only so validate.py can check ours is not copied from it.
